slides.0.title: Terroir Comparisons and Grape Profiles
slides.0.subtitle: Set against the world's classics
slides.1.title: A comparison frame: classify, then conclude
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Appearance
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Colour depth and hue (Xinomavro pale, quick to brick; Moschofilero pale lemon-pink)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Nose
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Aroma type: floral, citrus, stone fruit, mineral, resinous
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Palate
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Acidity, tannin, alcohol, body, sweetness from drying or fortification
slides.1.highlights.3.title: Conclusions
slides.1.highlights.3.content: Grape, region, quality and ageing potential, with clues as reasons
slides.1.content: Diploma tasting and essays both demand conclusions backed by evidence. This lesson organises the main Greek grapes into comparable clues.
slides.2.title: Whites: Assyrtiko in context
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Santorini Assyrtiko
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Intense minerality and salinity, very high acidity, dense structure
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Assyrtiko elsewhere
slides.2.highlights.1.content: More primary fruit, a less dense and lighter mineral structure
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Moschofilero
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Low alcohol, rose and jasmine, vibrant acidity; usually made in stainless steel
slides.2.highlights.3.title: Malagousia
slides.2.highlights.3.content: Peach, mango and citrus, with more body than Moschofilero
slides.2.content: Distinguishing clues: mineral and saline → Santorini Assyrtiko; rose + low alcohol → Moschofilero; peach and mango + fuller → Malagousia.
slides.3.title: Reds: Xinomavro vs Nebbiolo, Agiorgitiko's range
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Where Xinomavro resembles Nebbiolo
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Pale, high in acid and tannin, ageing over a decade, turning brick with age
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Differences
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Xinomavro grows in a warmer Mediterranean-influenced setting with different aromas and soils; frame comparisons as similar structure, different terroir
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Agiorgitiko's altitude gradient
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Lower sites riper and fuller; mid-slopes (about 450–650 m) most balanced; highest sites most aromatic and tense
slides.3.content: Avoid the shortcut "Xinomavro is Greece's Nebbiolo"; Diploma markers prefer answers that name both likenesses and differences.
slides.4.title: Sweet wines in context
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Vinsanto versus Mavrodaphne
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Muscat of Samos versus Muscat of Lemnos
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Samos uses Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains; Lemnos uses Muscat of Alexandria
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Useful identification clues
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Colour, oxidative notes, fortified spirit, aroma family (Muscat floral/grape)
slides.4.content: In sweet-wine blind tasting, first judge the source of sweetness (drying, fortification, aromatic variety), then subdivide.
slides.5.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge Check
Compared with Santorini, Assyrtiko from elsewhere is usually…
A. more fruit-forward with a less dense structure
Santorini shows the more pronounced minerality and salinity.
Which clue set best fits Moschofilero?
A. Rose and jasmine, low alcohol, vibrant acidity
Moschofilero is a low-alcohol aromatic white.
What is the best way to compare Xinomavro with Nebbiolo?
A. Name the similar structure and explain the terroir differences
The Diploma favours covering both likenesses and differences.
